metadata.title: B2 First Speaking Practice
metadata.description: Full B2 First Speaking exam practice with 2 complete rounds covering all 4 parts of the exam.

teacherNotes: This lesson simulates the complete B2 First Speaking exam with 2 rounds
Round 1: Part 1 (Interview) + Part 2 (Long Turn) + Part 3 (Collaborative Task) + Part 4 (Discussion)
Round 2: Different topics for additional practice
Each round takes approximately 14-16 minutes (same as real exam)
Encourage students to use a wide range of vocabulary and grammar structures
Time each section carefully to simulate exam conditions
Provide feedback on: fluency, vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, and interaction
Students should work in pairs for Parts 2-4

slides.title: B2 First Speaking Practice
slides.subtitle: Exam Simulation - Two Complete Rounds
slides.content: This lesson simulates the Cambridge B2 First Speaking exam with 2 complete rounds. Work with a partner and practice all 4 parts of the exam.
By the end of this practice, you will:
objectives: Complete 2 full rounds of the B2 First Speaking exam
Practice all 4 parts: Interview, Long Turn, Collaborative Task, and Discussion
Use a range of vocabulary and grammar structures
Improve fluency, pronunciation, and interaction skills

slides.title: Round 1 - Part 1: Interview
slides.content: Examiner: Good morning. I'm going to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's begin.
questions: Where are you from? Tell me a little about your hometown.
What do you enjoy doing in your free time?
Tell me about your family. Do you have any brothers or sisters?
What kind of music do you like? Why?
Do you prefer to spend time indoors or outdoors? Why?
tips: Give extended answers - don't just say one word
Include reasons and examples
Use a range of vocabulary
Speak clearly and at a natural pace

slides.title: Round 1 - Part 2: Long Turn
slides.prompt: In this part of the test, you're going to speak for 1 minute on your own. You'll have 1 minute to prepare.
slides.content: Task: Look at the two pictures. They show people shopping in different places. Compare the photos and answer this question: Why have people chosen to shop in these places?
tips: Use the 1 minute preparation time to make notes
Compare the two situations in the photos
Speculate about why people might choose each place
Use expressions for speculation: 'might be,' 'could be,' 'perhaps,' 'it seems that...'
Keep speaking for the full minute

slides.title: Round 1 - Part 3: Collaborative Task
slides.prompt: In this part, you and your partner will discuss a situation together. You have 2-3 minutes to discuss.
slides.content: Task: Look at the mind map. It shows different types of relationships. Talk to each other about what problems might arise in these relationships.
questions: Boyfriends and girlfriends
Parents and teenagers
Flatmates
Work colleagues
Brothers and sisters
tips: Respond to your partner's ideas and suggestions
Ask questions to keep the conversation going
Use phrases to agree and disagree politely
Try to reach a conclusion together

slides.title: Round 1 - Part 4: Discussion
slides.prompt: In this final part, the examiner will ask you to discuss some broader questions related to the topic.
slides.content: Examiner: Let's talk more generally about relationships and communication.
questions: Why are good relationships important in life?
What skills do you need to have good relationships with other people?
Some people say that technology has made relationships more difficult. What do you think?
How do relationships change as people get older?
What advice would you give to someone who is having problems with a friend or family member?
tips: Give longer, more developed answers
Use a range of complex structures
Include your opinion and justify it
Agree or disagree with other opinions

slides.title: Round 2 - Part 1: Interview
slides.content: Examiner: Let's talk about different topics. I'm going to ask you some questions.
questions: Tell me about your daily routine. What time do you usually get up?
What do you enjoy most about studying English?
Do you have any hobbies or interests that you're passionate about?
What kind of food do you enjoy eating? Why?
If you could change one thing about your town or city, what would it be?
tips: Give full, detailed answers
Use a variety of vocabulary and grammar structures
Include personal examples
Remember to speak clearly

slides.title: Round 2 - Part 2: Long Turn
slides.prompt: You'll have 1 minute to prepare and 1 minute to speak. Use the time to plan your response.
slides.content: Task: Look at the pictures. They show people doing different jobs. Compare the photos and answer this question: What do you think people might enjoy about these jobs?
tips: Make notes during preparation time
Compare the jobs shown in the photos
Speculate about what people might enjoy in each job
Use expressions for giving opinions and speculating
Try to use the full minute

slides.title: Round 2 - Part 3: Collaborative Task
slides.prompt: You and your partner have 2-3 minutes to discuss this situation together.
slides.content: Task: Look at the mind map. It shows different things that can contribute to happiness. Talk to each other about how important these are for our personal happiness.
questions: Listening to good music
Being physically fit
Having good friends
Doing a job you like
Having a lot of money
tips: Listen to your partner and respond to their points
Use phrases like: 'I see what you mean,' 'That's a good point,' 'On the other hand...'
Try to reach an agreement
Keep the conversation flowing naturally

slides.title: Round 2 - Part 4: Discussion
slides.prompt: Let's discuss the topic of work and careers more generally.
slides.content: Examiner: Let's talk more generally about work and careers.
questions: What factors do you think are most important when choosing a career?
Some people say that job satisfaction is more important than salary. What do you think?
How do you think careers will change in the future?
Is it better to have a job that is secure or a job that is interesting?
What advice would you give to someone starting their career?
tips: Give extended answers with examples
Use conditionals and advanced grammar structures
Express and justify opinions clearly
Engage with the examiner's questions

slides.content:
B2 First Speaking Assessment Criteria

  • Fluency and Coherence: Can speak at length, use connectors, and organize ideas
  • Lexical Resource: Uses a good range of vocabulary, including less common words
  • Grammatical Range and Accuracy: Uses a variety of structures with good control
  • Pronunciation: Is generally clear and uses appropriate intonation
  • Interactive Communication: Can initiate and respond, and keep the conversation going

Round 1 Topics

  • Part 1: Personal information, hobbies, family
  • Part 2: Shopping - comparing different places
  • Part 3: Problems in relationships
  • Part 4: Relationships and communication

Round 2 Topics

  • Part 1: Daily routine, studies, food
  • Part 2: Jobs - what people enjoy about work
  • Part 3: Factors contributing to happiness
  • Part 4: Work and careers

Image Sources

  • Round 1 Part 2: ShoppingPrt21.png (Why have people chosen to shop in these places?)
  • Round 1 Part 3: Relationships1.png (What problems might arise in these relationships?)
  • Round 2 Part 2: Turn2Jobs.png (What do you think people might enjoy about these jobs?)
  • Round 2 Part 3: Speaking3MindMap1.png (How important are these for our personal happiness?)

Timing Guide

  • Part 1: 3 minutes
  • Part 2: 2 minutes (1 minute preparation + 1 minute speaking)
  • Part 3: 3 minutes
  • Part 4: 4 minutes
  • Total per round: 12 minutes

Suggested Feedback

  • Note down good vocabulary and grammar usage
  • Identify areas for improvement
  • Provide specific examples from the student's responses
  • Encourage self-reflection after each round
